title: DR1 fills in the selected country's code as a fixed prefix and asks only for the part after it; the frontend asks the user to type the whole region of origin code into a field capped at five characters.

finding.frontend: Answering Yes reveals one text input labelled "Region of origin code", hinted "For example, FR-75", five characters wide and with no prefix shown. The user types the country part and the region part together, and the whole string is capped at five characters by src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/origin/controller.js:37 and :71-75, whose error reads "Region of origin code must be 5 characters or less". The example in the hint, FR-75, is itself exactly five characters, so any code with a longer region part cannot be entered.
finding.prototype: Answering Yes reveals a field labelled "Enter the region of origin code" hinted "Enter up to 5 characters.", with the selected country's code shown as a read-only prefix attached to the left of the input. The user types only the part after it and the prototype joins the two with a hyphen on submit. The prefix is looked up from the chosen country, so Ceuta (Spain) gives XC and Melilla (Spain) gives XL rather than the parent country's ES.
finding.difference: Split the field: show the selected country's code as a prefix and collect only the suffix, capping the suffix at five characters rather than the whole code. The stored value should still be the joined code, so nothing downstream needs to change shape. The prefix depends on knowing a code per country including the territories, which is where this meets the country-list finding — Ceuta and Melilla have their own prefixes, not their parent's. If the country control becomes a search box the prefix has to update as the search selection changes, not only on page load.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding a country prefix rendered beside the frontend's region-of-origin code input — the captured DOM at fe-origin shows a bare govuk-input with no govuk-input__prefix and no wrapper.
finding.verification: Ran the falsifier against both rendered DOMs. fe-origin's reveal holds <input class="govuk-input govuk-input--width-5" id="regionOfOriginCode" name="regionOfOriginCode"> with no wrapper and no prefix element; dr1-origin-of-the-import's reveal holds <div class="govuk-input__wrapper app-region-origin-code__affix"> containing <div class="govuk-input__prefix" id="region-of-origin-code-prefix"> and then <input id="region-of-origin-code-suffix" name="regionOfOriginCodeSuffix" maxlength="5">. Both labels and both hints are verbatim as quoted — "Region of origin code" / "For example, FR-75" against "Enter the region of origin code" / "Enter up to 5 characters.". Checked the Ceuta and Melilla claim against DR1's own prefix table, embedded in the captured page as app-country-search__prefixes: "Ceuta (Spain)":"XC" and "Melilla (Spain)":"XL", while their parents are "Spain":"ES" — so the claim that territories carry their own prefix rather than the parent's is right, and it is not true of every territory (Azores and Madeira both take PT, French Guiana takes FR). Verified the join by reading the prototype's origin POST at app/routes.js:9246-9251, which builds `${countryPrefix}-${regionOfOriginCodeSuffix}`. Re-resolved both citations: origin/controller.js:37 is REGION_CODE_MAX_LENGTH = 5 and :71-75 is the maxText rule using it, template.njk:24-34 is the govukInput block, and region-of-origin-code-input.html:14-30 is the wrapper, prefix and input. Confirmed the five-character arithmetic in the frontend slot: the hint's own example FR-75 is exactly five characters, so the cap admits it and admits nothing longer. Band checked — the split needs only the ISO codes already carried as the select's option values, so it can land ahead of the country-list work. CORRECT.
finding.correction: No claim falsified; every quoted string and every citation resolved. Two notes for whoever builds it, neither changing the slots. (1) DR1's prefix element carries aria-hidden="true", so a screen-reader user hears only the suffix and is never told what the code will be prefixed with. That is a defect in DR1 rather than a requirement, and the frontend should not reproduce it — the govuk-frontend prefix pattern has the same problem and the usual fix is to put the prefix in the hint as well. (2) The generalisation "the prefix is looked up from the chosen country" is right but the Ceuta and Melilla example is the exception, not the rule: nine of DR1's eleven territories take their parent's code — Azores and Madeira PT, Canary Islands ES, French Guiana, Guadeloupe, Martinique, Mayotte, Reunion and Saint Martin all FR — and only Ceuta and Melilla differ. The three Crown Dependencies each carry their own code, GG, JE and IM. The difference slot's dependency on the country-list finding is unaffected either way.

relatedTo.why: the prefix is looked up per country, and the territories DR1 adds carry their own codes
both change the same revealed field, so they are cheapest done in one pass
